```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr) # nolint: undesirable_function_linter.

here <- if (dir.exists("tutorials/")) "tutorials/" else "."
source(file.path(here, "shared", "checkers.R")) # nolint: undesirable_function_linter.

tutorial_options(
    exercise.checker = bios_checker,
    exercise.timelimit = 60L,
    exercise.reveal_solution = FALSE,
    exercise.startover = TRUE
)

# The oldest R the course material is tested against.
min_r_version <- "4.2.0"

# The packages installed in step 2.4 of the README.
required_packages <- c("learnr", "rmarkdown", "shiny", "knitr", "tidyverse")
```

## What this is

This short tutorial checks that you have done the **Preparations before class**
in the course README correctly, and that the tutorials we use in class will run
on your machine. It takes about a minute.

The fact that you are reading this page already tells us a lot: R started,
**rmarkdown**, **knitr**, **shiny** and **learnr** are installed, and your
browser can display a tutorial. The steps below check the rest.

Each step is a small R console with code already filled in.

- **Run Code** runs the code and shows the result.
- **Submit Answer** runs the code *and* checks it, then tells you whether that
  part of your installation is in order.
- **Start Over** restores the code to how it started.

Work through the steps in order. If one of them fails, read the message, fix
what it asks for (or ask for help), and press **Submit Answer** again.

## Step 1: R

The code below reports the version of R that is running this tutorial. Press
**Submit Answer**.

```{r r-version, exercise=TRUE, exercise.eval=TRUE}
getRversion()
```

```{r r-version-check}
if (getRversion() >= min_r_version) {
    TRUE
} else {
    sprintf(
        paste0(
            "You are running R %s, but the course material is tested with R %s and ",
            "newer. Install a newer R from https://cran.uib.no/, restart RStudio, ",
            "and run this check again."
        ),
        getRversion(), min_r_version
    )
}
```

## Step 2: RStudio

We work with R through RStudio, so this tutorial should have been started from
the R console *inside* RStudio, with the `BIOS-IN5410.Rproj` project open. Press **Submit Answer**.

```{r rstudio, exercise=TRUE, exercise.eval=TRUE}
Sys.getenv("RSTUDIO") == "1"
```

```{r rstudio-check}
if (isTRUE(.result)) {
    TRUE
} else {
    paste0(
        "This tutorial does not seem to be running inside RStudio. That is not ",
        "fatal, but in class we will assume you use it. Install RStudio from ",
        "https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/, open BIOS-IN5410.Rproj in ",
        "it, and start this check again from the RStudio R console. If you are ",
        "deliberately using another editor, you can ignore this step."
    )
}
```

## Step 3: Required packages

This checks the packages from step 2.4 of the README. Press **Submit Answer**.

```{r packages, exercise=TRUE, exercise.eval=TRUE}
required_packages[!required_packages %in% rownames(installed.packages())]
```

```{r packages-check}
if (length(.result) == 0L) {
    TRUE
} else {
    paste0(
        "These packages are not installed: ", paste(.result, collapse = ", "),
        ". Run install.packages(c(",
        paste0("\"", .result, "\"", collapse = ", "),
        ")) in the RStudio R console, wait for it to finish, then press Submit ",
        "Answer again."
    )
}
```

## Done

If every step above came back green, your installation is complete and the
class tutorials will run. Nothing else is required of you before class, except
the reading in step 1 of the README.

If something failed, make sure to get help before class.

To stop this tutorial, simply close the browser tab.
